Public Comments

  D. RESOLUTION NO. 20-59 – AMENDING THE FISCAL YEAR 2020-21
  OPERATING BUDGET TO APPROPRIATE UNALLOCATED COMMUNITY
  DEVELOPMENT BLOCK GRANT (CDBG) FUNDS FOR USE IN THE CITY
  HALL ELEVATOR MODERNIZATION PROJECT

  The City of San Gabriel initially received $80,000 from Community
  Development Block Grant (CDBG) funds for the City Hall Elevator
  Modernization Project. This budget amendment will appropriate an
  additional $51,740 from unallocated CDBG Funds to use for the City Hall
  Elevator Modernization Project and increase the available funds for the
  project to $131,740. With the approved allocation of CDBG funds, the City will
  have sufficient funds to complete the City Hall Modernization Project without
  impacting the General Fund.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that City Council adopt Resolution No. 20-59 amending
  the Fiscal Year 2020-21 Operating Budget to appropriate $51,740 in the
  unallocated CDBG funds for the City Hall Elevator Modernization – Account
  No. 122-800-53-97-602.

  E. VERTICAL BANNERS  REQUEST  –  SAN  GABRIEL  EDUCATIONAL
  FOUNDATION (SEF)

  The City has received a vertical banner request from the San Gabriel
  Educational Foundation (SEF) to hang twenty vertical street banners for the
  SEF district wide art project that displays “Dream. Imagine. Create.” in the
  Mission District for Spring of 2021. This will serve all students within the San
  Gabriel Unified School District from pre-kindergarten to twelfth grade and
  will invite students to develop and submit their print media artwork to the
  SEF organization for inclusion in a virtual art festival. From their submissions,
  twenty pieces will be screened and randomly chosen for reproduction into
  vertical street banners by the foundation. The exact dates will be verified and
  coordinated with City staff to ensure availability.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – November 17, 2020  3
   Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that City Council grant this annual request and authorize
  future art installations which would foster community engagement,
  collaboration in support of arts education and provide locally-produced
  public art display pieces.

  F. ADOPTION OF RESOLUTION NO. 20-60 OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE
  CITY OF SAN GABRIEL, CALIFORNIA, CONSENTING TO THE INCLUSION
  OF PROPERTIES WITHIN THE TERRITORY OF THE CITY IN THE
  CALIFORNIA STATEWIDE COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY
  (CSCDA) COMMERCIAL OPEN PROPERTY ASSESSED CLEAN ENERGY
  (PROGRAM)

  The California Statewide Communities Development Authority (CSCDA) was
  created in 1988, under California’s Joint Exercise of Powers Act, to provide
  California’s local governments with an effective tool for the timely financing
  of community-based public benefit projects. The consideration to adopt
  Resolution No. 20-60 authorizing the City’s participation in CSCDA Open
  PACE will enable commercial property owners to finance permanently-fixed
  renewable energy, energy efficiency, water efficiency, and seismic-
  strengthening improvements as well as electric vehicle charging
  infrastructure.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 20-60
  authorizing the City’s participation in CSCDA Open PACE, which will enable
  property owners to finance permanently-fixed renewable energy, energy
  efficiency, water efficiency, and seismic-strengthening improvements as well
  as electric vehicle charging infrastructure.

  G. LEASE-PURCHASE AGREEMENT TO REPLACE AND UPGRADE POLICE
  DEPARTMENT’S RADIO COMMUNICATION SYSTEM

  The San Gabriel Police Department’s radio communication system is over 15
  years old and in critical need of replacement. The radio system is an essential
  part of the public safety commitment and connects first responders with
  dispatchers, who relay information gathered from the community. It is an
  obsolete system, where hardware and software support are no longer offered
  by Motorola Solutions, or by other radio service vendors. Over the past year,
  the Police Department has dealt with several critical radio system failures due

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – November 17, 2020  4
   to its age. Since then, the department has faced persistent problems,
  especially in regards to the performance and reliability of the dispatch
  consoles, portables, mobiles and repeater systems. These issues have
  produced periods of erratic static and digitization noise transmitted through
  the radio communication system, creating an officer and public safety risk.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:
  1. Approve the Motorola Solutions Equipment Lease-Purchase Agreement
  No. 24909 to replace and upgrade the Police Department’s radio
  communication system in the amount of $812,494.56 and authorize the
  City Manager to execute all necessary documents;
  2. Waive formal bidding requirements in accordance with the San Gabriel
  Purchasing Policy and Municipal Code Section 34.35; and
  3. Adopt Resolution No. 20-61.

  H. FIRST QUARTER FINANCIAL REPORT AND BUDGET UPDATE FOR FISCAL
  YEAR 2020-21

  The First Quarter Financial Report summarizes the City’s financial position as
  of October 31, 2020 and focuses on the General Fund. Projects provided in
  this report are preliminary and conservative.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 20-62
  Amending the City’s Budgeted Appropriations for Fiscal Year 2020-21.

  I. APPROPRIATION OF FUNDS FOR ADVOCACY AND GRANT WRITING
  SERVICES  FOR  VALLEY  BOULEVARD  STREETSCAPE AND
  RECONSTRUCTION PROJECT

  In April 2020, the City Council approved a Professional Services Agreement
  with MNS Engineers for advocacy and grant writing services to seek funding
  through the California Natural Resources Agency, Urban Greening Grant for
  a Valley Boulevard Streetscape and Reconstruction Project. Funding was
  approved in the FY 2019-20 budget using Waste Management Account No.
  124-800-55-96-813 in an amount of $42,790. At year end, an unused balance
  remained of $28,855 but the funds were not formally carried over to Fiscal

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – November 17, 2020  5
   Year 2020-21. Staff is requesting the re-appropriation of remaining unused
  funds from Fiscal Year 2019-20 via the approval of Resolution No. 20-63.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 20-63
  amending the FY 2020-21 Budget to appropriate $28,855 to Acct No. 124-
  800-55-96-813 from the Waste Management Fund Balance with the
  corresponding transfers.

  5. PUBLIC HEARING

  A. 414-420 SOUTH SAN GABRIEL BOULEVARD PLANNING CASE NOS.
  ZC19-001 (ZONE CHANGE/PLANNED DEVELOPMENT OVERLAY ZONE,
  TMAP19-008 (TENTATIVE PARCEL MAP), AND MITIGATED NEGATIVE
  DECLARATION AND MITIGATION MONITORING AND REPORTING

  6. NEW BUSINESS

  A. CONSIDERATION OF AWARD OF NON-EXCLUSIVE TOWING SERVICE
  FRANCHISES

  Select the link below to access the Additional Background Material.

  Additional Background Material (Unsuccessful Proposals)

  The consideration of approval of a non-exclusive franchise agreement for
  vehicle tow services and establishing a franchise fee to recover actual and
  reasonable costs for administration of the towing program for the City of San
  Gabriel Police Department pursuant to San Gabriel Municipal Code Section
  70.40 and Vehicle Code Section 12110. The City Council will also consider
  awarding non-exclusive towing service franchises to Navarro’s Towing and
  Al’s Towing.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:
  1. Adopt Resolution No. 20-65 to establish the franchise fee and approve the
  form Tow Services Agreement;
  2. Grant a non-exclusive towing service franchise to Navarro’s Towing and
  Al’s Towing; and
  3. Authorize the City Manager to execute a Tow Services Agreement

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – November 17, 2020  7
   B. APPOINTMENT TO THE SAN GABRIEL VALLEY MOSQUITO ABATEMENT
  AND VECTOR CONTROL DISTRICT BOARD OF TRUSTEES

  The Mayor is responsible for appointing members of the City Council to serve
  on various local and regional committees and organization boards. In
  addition, it is necessary for the Council to take formal action to appoint a
  representative to the San Gabriel Valley Mosquito and Vector Control District
  Board of Trustees prior to the January 8, 2021 Board Meeting.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council appoint a representative to serve on
  the San Gabriel Valley Mosquito and Vector Control District Board of Trustees
  for a two-year term or a four-year term of office.

  C. CAMPAIGN CONTRIBUTION LIMITS PER ASSEMBLY BILL 571

  Assembly Bill 571, effective January 1, 2021, will establish individual campaign
  contribution limits for local agencies which have not adopted their own
  regulations. The City Council will consider whether to adopt regulations or
  default to the limitations set by this legislation.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council consider the following options:
  1. Follow state limits. Direct staff to draft a resolution adopting the state’s
  default contribution limits as stated in AB 571, with an effective date of
  January 1, 2021, for consideration at a future meeting. While taking no
  action would produce the same effect, actively adopting the provisions set
  in AB 571 would make clear for future reference the City Council’s
  intention, since at this time the City’s Municipal Code and resolution
  archives are silent on the matter.
  2. Set the City’s own limits. Direct staff to draft an ordinance for
  consideration by the City Council at a future meeting establishing
  campaign contribution limits lower or higher than the current State
  contribution limits of $4,700, per AB 571.

  7. PUBLIC COMMENT

  8. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

  The next Regular City Council meeting will be held on Tuesday, December 1,

MINUTES OF NOVEMBER 17, 2020
  REGULAR MEETING OF THE SAN GABRIEL CITY COUNCIL

CALL TO ORDER

Mayor Menchaca called the regular meeting of the San Gabriel City Council to order at
6:34 P.M. on Tuesday, November 17, 2020, with all Council Members and staff
participating by teleconference.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Vice Mayor Liao.

ROLL CALL

Council Members Present:  Tony Ding, John R. Harrington, Jason Pu, Vice Mayor
  Chin Ho Liao, and Mayor Denise Menchaca.
Council Members Absent:  None.
Staff Members Present:  City Manager Mark Lazzaretto, Assistant City
  Manager/Community Development Director Arminé
  Chaparyan, Assistant City Attorney Lloyd Pilchen,
  Community Services/Interim Mission Playhouse
  Director Rebecca Perez, Police Chief Eugene Harris,
  Chief City Clerk Sharon Clark, Public Works Director/City
  Engineer Greg de Vinck, Human Resources/Risk
  Management Director Edward Macias, Interim Finance
  Director Kenneth Louie, and Assistant City Clerk Marilyn
  Bonus.

ANNOUNCEMENTS

Chief City Clerk Clark provided information for the public on how to view the meeting and
submit comments, and how to request meeting agendas.

1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

  Hearing no objection, Mayor Menchaca announced the agenda order was approved.
2. PRESENTATIONS

  A. COVID-19 BRIEFING

  The presentation was made by City Manager Lazzaretto for Fire Chief Wallace and
  by Police Chief Harris.

3. PUBLIC COMMENT – None.

4. CONSENT CALENDAR

  Regarding Item 4G, Sue Fitzsimmons, San Gabriel Police Department Volunteer,
  provided comments in support of adopting Resolution No. 20-61 authorizing the

   Lease-Purchase Agreement for radio communication equipment for the Police
  Department.

  A motion was made by Vice Mayor Liao, seconded by Mayor Menchaca, to approve
  Consent Calendar Items 4A – 4I as presented.

  Motion approved Consent Calendar Items 4A – 4I as presented by a vote of 5-0 as
  follows:

  AYES:  DING, HARRINGTON, PU, LIAO, MENCHACA
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN:  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE

  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  The City Council approved:

  1. Minutes of the City Council Regular Meeting of October 20, 2020.
  2. Minutes of the City Council Special Meeting of October 27, 2020.

  B. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  The City Council approved the October 8, 2020, October 16, 2020, October 22,
  2020, and October 29, 2020, Registers of Demands and Warrants for the payment
  of City expenditures.

  C. CASH AND INVESTMENT REPORT – OCTOBER 2020
  The City Council received and filed the Cash and Investment Report for October

  D. RESOLUTION NO. 20-59 – AMENDING THE FISCAL YEAR 2020-21 OPERATING
  BUDGET TO APPROPRIATE UNALLOCATED COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT
  BLOCK GRANT (CDBG) FUNDS FOR USE IN THE CITY HALL ELEVATOR
  MODERNIZATION PROJECT

  The City Council adopted Resolution No. 20-59 amending the Fiscal Year 2020-
  21 Operating Budget to appropriate $51,740 in unallocated CDBG funds for the

  E. VERTICAL BANNERS REQUEST – SAN GABRIEL EDUCATIONAL FOUNDATION
  (SEF)

  The City Council granted the annual vertical banners request from the San Gabriel
  Educational Foundation and authorized future art installations which would foster
  community engagement, collaboration in support of arts education and provide
  locally-produced public art display pieces.

  F. ADOPTION OF RESOLUTION NO. 20-60 OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY
  OF SAN GABRIEL, CALIFORNIA, CONSENTING TO THE INCLUSION OF
  PROPERTIES WITHIN THE TERRITORY OF THE CITY IN THE CALIFORNIA
  STATEWIDE  COMMUNITY  DEVELOPMENT  AUTHORITY  (CSCDA)
  COMMERCIAL OPEN PROPERTY ASSESSED CLEAN ENERGY (PROGRAM)

  The City Council adopted Resolution No. 20-60 authorizing the City’s
  participation in CSCDA Open PACE, which will enable property owners to finance
  permanently-fixed renewable energy, energy-efficiency, water-efficiency, and

CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 2 of 7  November 17, 2020
   seismic-strengthening improvements as well as electric vehicle charging
  infrastructure.

  G. LEASE-PURCHASE AGREEMENT TO REPLACE AND UPGRADE POLICE

  The City Council:
  1. Approved Motorola Solutions Equipment Lease-Purchase Agreement No.
  24909 to replace and upgrade the Police Department’s radio communication

  2. Waived formal bidding requirements in accordance with San Gabriel
  Purchasing Policy and Municipal Code Section 34.35; and
  3. Adopted Resolution No. 20-61 authorizing the Lease-Purchase Agreement for

  Department.
  H. FIRST QUARTER FINANCIAL REPORT AND BUDGET UPDATE FOR FISCAL YEAR
  2020-21

  The City Council adopted Resolution No. 20-62 Amending the City’s Budgeted

  I. APPROPRIATION OF FUNDS FOR ADVOCACY AND GRANT WRITING
  SERVICES FOR VALLEY BOULEVARD STREETSCAPE AND RECONSTRUCTION
  PROJECT

  The City Council adopted Resolution No. 20-63 amending the FY 2020-21 Budget

5. PUBLIC HEARING

  A. 414-420 SOUTH SAN GABRIEL BOULEVARD PLANNING CASE NOS. ZC19-001
  (ZONE CHANGE/PLANNED DEVELOPMENT OVERLAY ZONE, TMAP19-008
  (TENTATIVE PARCEL MAP), AND MITIGATED NEGATIVE DECLARATION AND
  MITIGATION MONITORING AND REPORTING PROGRAM)
  APPLICANT: 1784 CAPITAL HOLDINGS, INCORPORATED

  The staff presentation was made by Senior Planner Mat Chang.

  Mayor Menchaca opened the public hearing.

  Judy Huie Mena provided comments in support of the project.

  Mayor Menchaca closed the public hearing.

  Land-Use Consultant Shane Swerdlow of Craig Lawson & Co., LLC, representing the
  applicant, presented a PowerPoint presentation and introduced project-team
  members Kelly McKone, 1784 Capital Holdings, LLC; Judith HeartSong, Artists &
  Makers Studios; Michelle Bach, EAPC Architects and Engineers; and Clare Look-
  Jaeger, LLG.

  Discussion included details on widening Gladys Avenue; pricing for tenants and
  no/low-cost options for community members; parking; artists and makers studios
  floor plans; elements to help activate the street; visibility of gallery space; artist

CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 3 of 7  November 17, 2020
   outreach; details of Floor Area Ratio (F.A.R.) variance; market study; density
  pursuant to the Zoning Code; impact fees; street maintenance; foot traffic sources;
  and timing for financing.

  There was a consensus of the City Council to direct staff to work with the developer
  to provide additional feasibility data and prepare a revised impact fee allocation
  schedule, for consideration at a future City Council meeting.

  A motion was made by Mayor Menchaca, seconded by Council Member Pu, to
  reopen the public hearing and continue it to the January 19, 2021, regular City Council
  Meeting. Following additional discussion, Council Member Pu withdrew his second; and
  a motion was made by Mayor Menchaca, seconded by Vice Mayor Liao, to reopen the
  public hearing and continue it to the December 15, 2020, regular City Council Meeting.

  Motion carried by a vote of 5-0 as follows:
  AYES:  DING, HARRINGTON, PU, LIAO, MENCHACA
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN:  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE

Mayor Menchaca announced a health break at 8:46 P.M. and resumed the meeting at 9:00
P.M.

6. NEW BUSINESS

  A. CONSIDERATION OF AWARD OF NON-EXCLUSIVE TOWING SERVICE
  FRANCHISES

  The staff presentation was made by Police Captain Fabian Valdez.

  The following provided comments in support of awarding a towing franchise to
  Dickson Motor Service: Gary Watt, resident; Jay; Regina Bory; Alexis Salamanca,
  resident and business owner; Wendy Holten, resident; Michelle ChiuTse; Tracy R.
  Wilke; and Sandy Rosco, Executive Director of the San Gabriel Chamber of
  Commerce.

  Sean McMorris, resident, provided comments in support of a competitive process
  to award contracts and in support of awarding the towing service franchises to the
  recommended companies; and requested consideration of a hardship waiver policy
  for those who cannot afford to pay impound fees.

  Mike Gatto, representing Al’s Towing, clarified several elements of their proposal.

  Brian Martinez, CEO of Brian’s Toledo Towing Service Inc., provided comments
  appealing the staff recommendation of which companies to be awarded the non-
  exclusive towing franchises.

  The following provided comments in support of the selection of Al’s Towing for a
  non-exclusive towing franchise award: Christina Moore; Andy and Roberta Nunez,
  residents; Yvonne Belmontes, resident; and Erica Berge, resident.

  Jose A. Pavon, President of Al’s Towing, provided comments expressing his
  appreciation of the staff’s recommendation to award his company a non-exclusive
  towing franchise.

CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 4 of 7  November 17, 2020
   Cheryl Cabot provided comments in support of the staff recommendation to award
  non-exclusive towing franchises to Navarro’s Towing and Al’s Towing.

  Discussion included clarification that this award is only for Police Department use;
  methodology of the selection process; rating criteria details; benefits and
  drawbacks of having a rotation between several companies; having a trial period
  for several companies; methodology for the franchise fee; and the location of
  company facilities.

  A motion was made by Council Member Harrington, seconded by Mayor

  Gabriel business license as of the RFP date and having their primary towing
  yard in San Gabriel.
  3. Authorize the City Manager to execute a Tow Services Agreement between the
  City and each approved tow service operator.

  AYES:  DING, HARRINGTON, PU, LIAO, MENCHACA

  ABSTAIN:  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE

  B. APPOINTMENT TO THE SAN GABRIEL VALLEY MOSQUITO ABATEMENT AND

  The staff presentation was made by Assistant City Clerk Marilyn Bonus.

  C. CAMPAIGN CONTRIBUTION LIMITS PER ASSEMBLY BILL 571

  The staff presentation was made by Chief City Clerk Sharon Clark.

  Sean McMorris, resident, provided comments in favor of the adoption of campaign
  contribution limits lower than state limits.
  Discussion included that choosing state limits relieves the City of the burden of
  administration and enforcement and any undue influence; and clarification on the
  date window that defines each election.

  There was a consensus of the City Council to direct staff to draft a resolution
